items.prompt: ONE original wide 16:9 Japanese junior-high mathematics textbook illustration. In a stationery shop, TWO uniformed first-year junior-high students group plain gift packages by SOLID SHAPE on a shelf: rectangular boxes, upright cylinders with circular tops, and clearly TRIANGULAR PYRAMIDS (tetrahedra with four triangular faces, not square pyramids, prisms or cones). Use plain blue/green/orange wrapping with no patterns that disguise faces. One student moves a triangular-pyramid package to a matching group while the other thoughtfully compares a box and cylinder. All packages visible with clear straight edges or curved cylinder sides. Soft friendly watercolor/flat editorial style, fine outlines, simple readable background, original art. No text, numbers, labels, logos, price tags, equations or pseudo-writing anywhere. One finished image.
items.editPrompt: Correct ONLY the ORANGE packages to be unambiguous TRIANGULAR PYRAMIDS (regular tetrahedra). Each package has exactly FOUR triangular faces, FOUR vertices, SIX edges and a TRIANGULAR base. Do not draw Egyptian square-base pyramids. Rotate the girl's held orange package so one complete triangular face/base with THREE corners is clearly visible, with the fourth apex behind it and straight edges linking it to those three corners. Show some shelf packages resting on a triangular face with their other three triangular faces meeting at one point, not with any square/diamond base. Preserve the blue rectangular boxes, green cylinders, both students, their expressions, shelf, composition and watercolor style. No words, numbers, labels, dotted mathematical annotations or logos.

items.prompt: ONE original wide 16:9 Japanese junior-high math textbook chapter-challenge illustration. THREE uniformed students at a desk compare PAPER MODELS of a cylinder, a cone, and a regular cube with flat paper pieces and folded nets used to assemble them. All models have geometrically recognizable simple forms: cylinder circular ends and curved side, cone circular base and one apex, cube square faces and straight edges. A clearly unlabelled cylinder net (rectangle plus two equal circles) is laid flat; other net papers are partly folded in the students' hands, with tabs, so this is a construction scene rather than an invented precise solved diagram. Show students looking between the flat paper and the models. Soft friendly watercolor/flat style, fine outlines, subdued blue/green/orange, simple classroom background, original art. No text, numbers, vertex labels, equations, logos, ruler numerals or fake writing anywhere. One finished image.
items.editPrompt: Correct ONLY BOTH white CUBE NETS: the one held by the left student and the one lying on the front-left table. They currently have five square faces, which is wrong. Each cube net must have exactly SIX equal square faces in a VALID cross net: FOUR squares connected in a straight vertical column, plus ONE square to the left and ONE to the right of the SECOND square in that column (4+1+1=6). Include folding tabs outside these six faces, but tabs do not count as faces. The held net should have all six faces visibly connected. Reduce and reposition the table net slightly if needed so ALL SIX faces fit within the image without covering the cube/cone models. Preserve all three students, cube/cylinder/cone models, existing cylinder rectangle and its two circles, cone sector papers, faces, lighting, composition and style. No letters, numbers, measurement labels or logos. All six squares must be individually visible; do not add a seventh square or disconnect one.
